themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in CD 210 spiked to 17 THIS WEEK, a 172% increase above the 8-week baseline of 6.2 complaints per week, with no clear cause identified—warranting investigation into whether construction, venue activity, or infrastructure work is driving the spike.
evidence: 17 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (172% spike, z-score 7.72)
Noise - Residential remains top 5 complaint type overall (702 complaints over 90 days)
No corresponding Reddit discussions or news coverage suggests localized, unreported issue
reporting_angles: Call 311 complaint filers to identify common source(s)—specific address, time of day, type of noise
Check DOB permits for active construction sites; cross-reference with noise complaint locations

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped to 11 THIS WEEK, a 780% spike above the 8-week baseline of 1.2 per week (z-score 8.95)—suggesting a sudden sanitation failure, likely tied to building-level or neighborhood trash management breakdown.
evidence: 11 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (780% spike, z-score 8.95)
Unsanitary Condition also in top 10 overall complaints (220 over 90 days), suggesting endemic sanitation issues
Community board has zero recent sanitation-focused budget requests despite spike
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY on whether collection routes were changed, delayed, or diverted THIS WEEK
Canvass multi-unit buildings in high-complaint zones—are garbage compactors broken, overflow bins overflowing, or service stopped?

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Illegal Removal
themes_detail.summary: Two tree-related spikes converged: Dead/Dying Tree complaints hit 5 two weeks ago (1900% above baseline), and Illegal Tree Damage jumped to 3 THIS WEEK (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)—suggesting possible storm damage followed by unauthorized removal or systemic neglect.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% spike, z-score 10.97)
Illegal Tree Damage: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Community board's repeated budget request for park upgrades suggests existing tree infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Check NYC Parks maintenance logs for recent work orders or service reductions in CD 210
Interview Parks enforcement on whether illegal tree cutting/removal enforcement has been triggered by these complaints

themes_detail.label: Plumbing System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK, a 433% increase above the 8-week baseline of 0.8 per week (z-score 3.92), converging with 1,411 Heat/Hot Water complaints over 90 days—suggesting water system infrastructure stress affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: Plumbing complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 3.92)
Heat/Hot Water dominates 90-day complaints (1,411 total), second only to Illegal Parking (2,793)
Water System complaints also in top 10 (214 over 90 days), indicating ongoing water infrastructure fragility
reporting_angles: Interview DEP on whether water main breaks, pressure drops, or service interruptions occurred THIS WEEK in Throgs Neck/Co-op City
Check if plumbing spike correlates geographically with Heat/Hot Water complaints—may indicate boiler/supply system failure

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street-condition complaints (Curb Condition, Street Sweeping) show paired spikes: Curb Condition up 700% THIS WEEK (z-score 5.42) and Street Sweeping up 2300% three weeks ago (z-score 8.69)—suggesting deferred street maintenance and possible sanitation route failures.
evidence: Curb Condition: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Street Sweeping: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Street Condition in top 10 overall (591 over 90 days); Illegal Parking dominates at 2,793, compounding street management issues
reporting_angles: Request DSNY street sweeping schedule for CD 210—has coverage been reduced or routes consolidated?
Visit curbs with high complaint density to document pot holes, crumbling asphalt, or debris accumulation
